paragraphs.title: Personal Responsibility Instead of Inherited Guilt

answers: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge
The children have eaten bread, and the fathers are satisfied
The righteous shall walk in the way, and the wicked shall fall
easy.explanation: This is the proverb quoted in Ezekiel 18:2.
easy.q: What proverb were the people using concerning Israel?

answers: The fathers only
The Lord
The king
easy.explanation: The Lord says, "Behold, all souls are mine."

answers: It becomes wealthy
It inherits its fathers
It shall die
easy.explanation: The verse says, "the soul that sinneth, it shall die."
easy.q: What happens to the soul that sins?

answers: That children are punished for the sins of their fathers
That people should practice righteousness
That judgment is important
medium.explanation: The passage teaches that each person is accountable for his or her own sin.
medium.q: What idea does the Lord reject through His response to the proverb?

answers: Fruit that is sweet and ripe
Fruit with a sharp, unpleasant taste
Dry bread
medium.explanation: Sour grapes are grapes with an unpleasantly sharp taste.
medium.q: In the proverb, what does "sour grapes" refer to?

answers: Because every soul belongs to God, each person is accountable before Him
Because fathers determine the fate of their children
Because only children are judged
medium.explanation: God's ownership of every soul emphasizes individual accountability.
medium.q: How are the statements "all souls are mine" and "the soul that sinneth, it shall die" related?

answers: Family history always determines a person's fate
Human actions have no importance
A person cannot rely on inherited blame instead of accepting personal responsibility
challenge.explanation: God replaces the proverb of inherited blame with the principle of personal responsibility.
challenge.q: What central idea emerges from the movement from the proverb to God's words?

answers: To show that each stands individually before the Lord
To show that the son is always punished for his father
To show that the father is not responsible for his own actions
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the father and son as distinct souls belonging to God.
challenge.q: Why does the Lord mention both the soul of the father and the soul of the son?

answers: A person's actions matter
A son always bears his father's iniquity
Sin belongs to the soul that commits it
challenge.explanation: The passage directly rejects the idea that the son always bears the father's sin.
challenge.q: Which conclusion does not agree with these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Person and the Wicked Son

answers: He does that which is lawful and right
He commits robbery and oppression
He worships idols only
easy.explanation: The passage says that the just man does what is lawful and right.
easy.q: What does the just man do at the beginning of the passage?

answers: To the king
To the hungry
To his wealthy neighbor
easy.explanation: He has given his bread to the hungry.
easy.q: To whom does the righteous man give his bread?

answers: He keeps all the Lord's statutes
He covers the naked with a garment
He commits violence, oppression, and abominations
easy.explanation: The son is described as a robber who commits many wicked acts.
easy.q: What does the wicked son do?

answers: Faith, morality, and financial relationships
Warfare, trade, and farming
Music, poetry, and construction
medium.explanation: The passage addresses idolatry, moral conduct, and treatment of the poor and indebted.
medium.q: In what areas is the righteous man's conduct described?

answers: A gift
Interest charged on a loan
An offering of charity
medium.explanation: Usury refers to interest taken from money lent to another person.
medium.q: In this context, what does "usury" mean?

answers: Because he chooses to commit wicked acts himself
Because he does not know his father
Because he is wealthy
medium.explanation: The description focuses on the son's own actions and choices.
medium.q: Why is the wicked son judged independently?

answers: Righteousness is only a matter of belief
Righteousness includes both faithfulness to God and moral conduct
Charity has no connection with judgment
challenge.explanation: The righteous man avoids idols and also acts justly toward other people.
challenge.q: What does the combination of devotion to God and treatment of the poor teach about the righteous man?

answers: The righteous man restores pledges and avoids violence, while the son oppresses and fails to restore the pledge
Both of them take usury
The righteous man refuses bread to the hungry, while the son feeds them
challenge.explanation: The righteous man protects the needy, while the wicked son uses violence and withholds what is owed.
challenge.q: What especially distinguishes the righteous man from the wicked son in financial matters?

answers: To contrast a faithful way of life with a way of abominations
To prove that all sons are righteous
To remove the need for judgment
challenge.explanation: The two descriptions create a clear contrast between righteousness and wickedness.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of presenting the righteous man before the wicked son?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Son Does Not Bear His Father's Guilt

answers: All his father's sins
All his father's riches
All his father's praises
easy.explanation: The son sees all the sins that his father has committed.
easy.q: What does the son see in his father?

answers: He does the same things as his father
He does not do the same things as his father
He hides his father's actions
easy.explanation: The son considers his father's conduct and does not do such things.
easy.q: What does the son choose to do?

answers: He dies for his father's iniquity
He is judged only by his family
He shall surely live
easy.explanation: The Lord says that the son "shall surely live."
easy.q: What happens to the righteous son?

answers: He can see his father's sins and refuse to imitate them
His father is actually righteous
He has no ability to choose
medium.explanation: The passage explicitly says that the son considers his father's sins and does not do likewise.
medium.q: What enables a son raised in a wicked home to choose another way?

answers: The father's sin and guilt
The father's righteousness
The father's wealth
medium.explanation: Iniquity refers to the wrongdoing committed by the father.
medium.q: What does the phrase "the iniquity of his father" mean?

answers: They receive the same judgment
The father dies in his iniquity, while the son lives in righteousness
The son is punished while the father is rescued
medium.explanation: The father is judged for his own sin, but the righteous son does not bear it.
medium.q: How are the father and son treated in judgment?

answers: Family background determines judgment
Each person is judged according to his own way and actions
A son is always guilty of his father's actions
challenge.explanation: The father is judged for his deeds, and the son is judged according to his own choice.
challenge.q: What principle is shared by the accounts of the father and the son?

answers: It shows that a family environment does not force a person to sin
It shows that sin is inherited
It shows that there is no difference between the righteous and wicked
challenge.explanation: Although the son sees his father's sins, he chooses not to follow them.
challenge.q: Why does the example of a righteous son in a wicked household strengthen the teaching about personal responsibility?

answers: The son's righteousness erases the father's sins
The son bears his father's iniquity but receives life
The son does not bear his father's iniquity, and each person is judged according to his own way
challenge.explanation: The passage plainly teaches that the father and son bear responsibility for their own conduct.
challenge.q: Which statement best summarizes these verses?

answers: He shall surely live
He is punished for his righteousness
He remains wicked forever
easy.explanation: The Lord says that the wicked person who turns shall live.
easy.q: What happens to the wicked man who turns from all his sins?

answers: His past righteousness saves him
He shall die in his sin
He becomes more righteous
easy.explanation: His former righteousness is not mentioned, and he dies in his sin.
easy.q: What happens to a righteous person who turns away from righteousness and commits iniquity?

answers: According to his ways
According to his wealth
According to his family alone
easy.explanation: The Lord says, "I will judge you... every one according to his ways."
easy.q: According to what does the Lord judge each person?

answers: He keeps God's statutes and does what is lawful and right
He continues in all his abominations
He stops doing judgment and righteousness
medium.explanation: Repentance is shown by turning from sin and doing what is lawful and right.
medium.q: What changes in the wicked man when he turns?

answers: Acts of rebellion or wrongdoing
Acts of righteousness
Words of wisdom
medium.explanation: Transgressions are sinful violations of God's commands.
medium.q: What does the word "transgressions" mean in this passage?

answers: Because God judges according to the person's present way
Because righteousness is forbidden
Because the past is more important than the present
medium.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the person's current sinful way determines the judgment.
medium.q: Why do a righteous person's former deeds not save him when he turns to wickedness?

answers: The past alone determines judgment
A change in a person's way changes his standing in judgment
No one can change
challenge.explanation: Turning from wickedness or turning to wickedness affects the judgment described in the passage.
challenge.q: What principle is shared by the wicked person who repents and the righteous person who falls?

answers: God desires the death of the wicked
God prefers that the wicked remain in his way
God does not desire the wicked person's death but wants him to return and live
challenge.explanation: The question points to God's desire for repentance and life rather than death.
challenge.q: What does the question, "Have I any pleasure at all that the wicked should die?" reveal about repentance?

answers: He says that Israel's ways are unequal, not His way
He agrees that there is no judgment
He removes personal responsibility
challenge.explanation: The Lord asks whether His way is not equal and declares that Israel's ways are unequal.
challenge.q: How does the Lord answer the claim, "The way of the Lord is not equal"?

paragraphs.title: A Call to Change, Renewal, and Life

answers: From all their transgressions
From all their joys
From all God's statutes
easy.explanation: The Lord commands Israel to repent and turn from all its transgressions.
easy.q: From what does the Lord call Israel to turn?

answers: A new house
A new heart and a new spirit
New wealth
easy.explanation: The Lord says, "make you a new heart and a new spirit."
easy.q: What does the Lord tell Israel to make?

answers: Turn and live
Hide the transgressions
Remain in the former way
easy.explanation: The passage ends with the command, "turn yourselves, and live ye."
easy.q: What is the concluding command of the passage?

answers: Cast away transgressions, make a new heart and spirit, and live
Continue in sin, complain, and die
Punish others, hide, and return to sin
medium.explanation: The verses describe rejecting sin, receiving inner renewal, and choosing life.
medium.q: What order of action is presented in the call to change?

answers: An inward change that turns a person away from sin
A different physical organ
A change in a person's name
medium.explanation: The phrase describes spiritual and moral renewal.
medium.q: What does the phrase "a new heart" mean in this context?

answers: Because He takes pleasure in death
Because He has no pleasure in the death of the one who dies
Because Israel's actions have no meaning
medium.explanation: God says He has no pleasure in death and therefore calls Israel to turn and live.
medium.q: Why does the Lord call Israel to turn?

answers: Repentance involves inward change, not merely an outward statement
Repentance means keeping all one's sins
Repentance means changing location only
challenge.explanation: The language of a new heart and spirit emphasizes inner renewal.
challenge.q: How does "a new heart and a new spirit" relate to repentance?

answers: People are responsible for their ways and can turn to a new way of life
People cannot change their ways
Only a person's ancestors can repent
challenge.explanation: Personal responsibility includes the ability to turn from sin and live.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between "I will judge you... according to your ways" and "turn yourselves, and live ye"?

answers: To increase punishment
To remain in transgression
To turn from transgression and live
challenge.explanation: The passage connects turning away from sin with life.
challenge.q: What goal is presented at the end of the call to Israel?
